summary: Bietigheim-Bissingen owns eight inner-city and station garages itself (Mobilitätsplan 2035, March 2023) rather than running them through the Stadtwerke, and the central garages charge 0.10 euro an hour; in May 2025 the city justified this as retail support against free parking at Breuningerland Ludwigsburg, while saying the garages are not profitable (subsidy about 285,000 euros in 2020). On-street parking in the centre is free but time-limited (about 500 public spaces versus about 240 paid garage spaces in 2023), and the only resident parking so far is the zone around the hospital (since February 2016), because 2013 and 2018 surveys found Innenstadt occupancy too low to justify it. The Mobilitätsplan 2035, approved by the Gemeinderat in March 2023, lists parking-management concepts for the Innenstadt and station area, renovation of the Farbstraße, Turmstraße and Bahnhof garages (rough estimate about 10 million euros) and extensions to the parking guidance system as measures. Since 2025 the budget crisis has put fees on the agenda: in July 2025 the council did not raise them, in December 2025 the mayor announced a proposal, and in August 2026 he said fees will come, possibly from 2027, first for the Altstadt and a ring around the core. The station P+R was described as nearly full (about 700 spaces) in the 2023 plan, while Ellental was about 25 percent used.

items.text: Resident parking around the hospital has existed since February 2016, following a Gemeinderat approval in late 2014 after a study found heavy visitor and patient pressure. About half the spaces are reserved for permit holders, the rest need a parking disc from 8:00 to 20:00 with a 6-hour maximum, and the permit costs 60 euros for 2 years.
items.source_title: Bewohnerparken im Bereich Krankenhaus - Stadt Bietigheim-Bissingen

items.text: The administration asked the Gemeinderat to approve the Mobilitätsplan 2035 and the draft Maßnahmen-Fahrplan at its session of 21 March 2023 (paper dated 10 March 2023); a city press release of 5 April 2023 describes the plan as recently adopted by the Gemeinderat. The paper states no concrete costs arise at first, and cost-relevant measures must come back to the council individually.
items.source_title: Drucksache GR 25.1/2023: Mobilitätsplan 2035 mit Maßnahmen-Fahrplan - Beschluss

items.text: The draft Maßnahmen-Fahrplan (status 10 March 2023) schedules parking concepts with Parkraumbewirtschaftung, Bewohnerparken and Parkraummanagement for the Innenstadt and for the station area (Aurain, Buch-Nordwest, Lothar-Späth-Carré, Bogenviertel) as short-term measures (2023-2024), and for the Bissinger Ortsmitte and residential/commercial areas as medium-term (2025-2028). It also lists renovation of the Farbstraße, Turmstraße and Bahnhof garages (2023-2028), neighbourhood garages with charging in Aurain-Carré and Bogenviertel, a dynamic Parkleitsystem in Ellental, a new one in Bissingen, and a mobile-parking concept (all medium-term).

The Mobilitätsplan reports that surveys in 2013 and 2018 found garage and car-park occupancy in the Innenstadt too low to meet the legal conditions for Bewohnerparken, partly because of the new Farbstraße car park. It also notes the Innenstadt already has a dynamic parking guidance system showing available spaces in real time.

The Mobilitätsplan lists eight city-owned garages (Kreuzstraße, Flößerstraße, Meierhofstraße, Farbstraße, Turmstraße, Löchgauer Straße, Kreuzäcker/Ellental and Bahnhofsplatz). The city's subsidy for them was about 235,000 euros in 2018 and 285,000 euros in 2020 (roughly 400 and 480 euros per space a year), and a first rough estimate puts renovating Farbstraße, Turmstraße and Bahnhof at about 10 million euros, or about 1 million a year if spread over 10 years.

The Mobilitätsplan counts about 500 free, time-limited public spaces on open car parks along the Parkring in the Innenstadt and about 240 paid spaces in public garages, and says the garages are not fully used. For park-and-ride it reports about 700 spaces at the station, described as nearly full, and 90 at Ellental, about 25 percent used according to the VVS.

As of 1 July 2021 the city's price list showed 0.10 euro an hour, day and night, in the Kreuzstraße/Flößerstraße/Meierhofstraße, Farbstraße/Turmstraße and Löchgauer Straße garages, with monthly passes of 20 to 35 euros (daytime) or 40 to 50 euros (day and night). The Bahnhofsplatz garage charged 1 euro up to 2 hours and 3 euros a day, and Kreuzäcker (Ellental) 0.10 euro an hour up to 5 hours and 2 euros a day.
items.source_title: Parken in Bietigheim-Bissingen, Stand 01.07.2021 (Entgelte aller Parkhäuser)

items.text: The same 2021 city price list states that the Stuttgarter Straße garage has been run by Bahnpark/Contipark since 1 January 2017, and that the Borsigstraße 'West' garage opened on 1 November 2017 and is owned and operated by Bietigheimer Wohnbau GmbH rather than the city.
items.source_title: Parken in Bietigheim-Bissingen, Stand 01.07.2021 (Entgelte aller Parkhäuser)

items.text: In February 2024 the Bietigheimer Zeitung reported about 1,000 public spaces near the Bietigheim inner city, most of them free, and a city subsidy for the garages of about 285,000 euros in 2020. A parking concept for the inner city is planned, but no date had been set for discussing parking management and it was unclear whether fewer spaces would remain.

In May 2025 three city-run central garages still charged 0.10 euro an hour with parking allowed up to 48 hours. City spokesperson Anette Hochmuth said the garages are not profitable, are a measure to support retail, and compete with free parking at Breuningerland Ludwigsburg.
items.source_title: Parkhäuser in Bietigheim-Bissingen: Parken für zehn Cent die Stunde mitten in der Innenstadt - wie kann das sein?

items.text: During the July 2025 supplementary budget (more than 11.5 million euros missing in the 2025 operating budget) the Gemeinderat raised Kita fees by 10 percent a year for five years but did not decide any parking-fee increase. The paper reports the parking topic is due to return to the agenda, and a Green councillor criticised that families are burdened while parking stays cheap.
items.source_title: Finanzlage in Bietigheim: Stadt setzt Prioritäten in Not: Parken bleibt günstig, Kita-Gebühren steigen

items.text: In the December 2025 budget debate SPD and GAL jointly asked for parking fees to be introduced or raised, and Oberbürgermeister Jürgen Kessing said a proposal based on an existing concept would be brought to the council after coordination with the Aktive Unternehmer business group. The 2026 budget was approved with a deficit of just under 15 million euros; no fee decision is reported.

In an interview published 21 August 2026 Oberbürgermeister Kessing said the city 'will not avoid introducing parking fees'. He said timing is still to be discussed with the Gemeinderat (possibly from 2027), no amounts were named, and fees would apply first to the Altstadt and a ring around the core, with Buch and Bissingen possibly later. This is a stated intention, not an adopted rule.

In January 2025 the public car park at Wilhelmstraße/Stuttgarter Straße (B 27) next to the planned Aurain-Carré was closed for a few days for tree felling. The development plans foresee a parking garage on that site, but Bietigheimer Wohnbau planned to build a residential building on Austraße first (start expected early 2026), so the car park was expected to stay in use for some time.
items.source_title: Parkplätze in Bietigheim-Bissingen: Sperrung nur kurzzeitig, Parkplatz in Bietigheim wohl noch Jahre nutzbar

items.text: Stadtwerke Bietigheim-Bissingen reported 18 public charging locations in the city after six new ones, with 150 kW fast chargers at the EgeTrans Arena, Buchzentrum and Rötestraße. About 504,000 kWh were charged at its Bietigheim-Bissingen sites in the previous year (2023), and the new 11 kW columns cost about 10,000 euros net each; the release names no garage sites.
items.source_title: Pressemitteilung Stadtwerke Bietigheim-Bissingen: Lade Netz für E-Mobilisten wächst

items.text: DB's station page (read 21 October 2026, undated) lists the DB BahnPark Parkhaus Süd on Stuttgarter Straße with 291 spaces at 1 euro an hour and 3.50 euros a day. It also lists a covered P+R at 1 euro for 2 hours and 3 euros for 24 hours, a 200-space garage 'Sky' at Borsigstraße 2 (5 a.m. to 11 p.m., 5 euros for 24 hours) and a 22-space open lot; operators other than DB BahnPark are not named.

gaps: No Gemeinderat vote on the announced parking-fee proposal (SPD/GAL motion, December 2025; mayor's interview August 2026) and no adopted Parkraumkonzept Innenstadt or Bewohnerparken for the Innenstadt found; the fee level, scope and start date are still open in the sources read.
No current official tariff list for the city garages after the 1 July 2021 list; the 2025 press reports confirm 0.10 euro an hour but I found no city page confirming it for 2026.

No usage or occupancy statistics for the city garages or the Parkleitsystem after the 2023 Mobilitätsplan, and no go-live date for the Innenstadt guidance system; status of the Farbstraße/Turmstraße/Bahnhof renovations after 2023 not found.

Stuttgarter Zeitung article of 9 July 2026 on the start of construction at Aurain-Carré is paywalled (only the lead was readable), so the garage plans there could not be confirmed: https://www.stuttgarter-zeitung.de/lokales/ludwigsburg/umstrittenes-projekt-mehr-als-200-wohnungen-in-bietigheim-aurain-carre-wird-nun-gebaut-79267233.html

Further council papers found in search but not opened: GR 81/2023 Maßnahmenfahrplan and Steckbriefe (https://www.bietigheim-bissingen.de/fileadmin/user_upload_stadtverwaltung/seitenstruktur/wirtschaft-einkaufen-verkehr/verkehr-und-mobilitaet/GR_81-2023_Ma%C3%9Fnahmenfahrplan.pdf and .../GR_81-2023_Steckbriefe.pdf), which may hold the detailed parking measures.

Details of the Löchgauer Straße garage (80 spaces, opened 2017, tariffs 1 euro per 10 hours) appear only in Heidelberg24 (https://www.heidelberg24.de/deutschland/baden-wuerttemberg/guenstigstes-parkhaus-deutschland-bietigheim-autofahrer-parken-preise-tarif-tiefgarage-zr-93731275.html) and t-online, which I did not use as support; individual garage capacities from an official source were not found.

The Stadtwerke Bietigheim-Bissingen appear only as charging-network operator; no Stadtwerke role in garage operation was found, and no shopping-centre garage (for example Kronenzentrum) data was found. Parking enforcement, Umweltzone and event parking (Pferdemarkt, EgeTrans Arena) not covered.

The DB station page is undated and the 'Sky' garage operator is not named; the Contipark page for the station garage (https://www.contipark.de/de/parken/bietigheim-bissingen/parkhaus-stuttgarter-strasse/) was opened but not used.
